items.q: What three losses make a breakup grief?
items.a: The **future you expected**, the person you thought they were, and **who you were with them**. He says you miss the **hoped-for version** and the promised future, not the week-to-week record.

items.q: What test replaces the moving-in story?
items.a: **Safe, seen, and supported.** Plans (a dog, a wedding) are not the relationship. He says most people he coaches find **two of the three** were missing.

items.q: Why does repeating the story feel necessary?
items.a: He compares it to a **washing machine**. Breakups, he says, hit the same brain regions as **drug withdrawal**. Stalking and replaying strengthen the loop. **Block, mute, delete**, then move and do new mental work.
That you **cared**, not that you were meant to be. Take **responsibility without all the blame**. Make a ritual: burn an unsent letter, bury a photo, or delete the thread and **walk with no phone**.
